Subject: Observability custody for private enclave — telemetry collector proposal

Hi Kimberly,

We’re kicking off the telemetry plan for the new private deployment (enclave) and need guidance on how Redwood recommends we handle logs, metrics and traces so we can remain compliant with our SOC2 controls. A few specific asks: 

- Can Redwood run a managed forwarder inside our VPC enclave, or do you recommend we run a customer-owned collector (sidecar/daemonset)?
- What does chain-of-custody look like for artifacts (raw logs, processed traces) — is there a minimal audit trail you can provide?
- We need a short acceptance checklist for our Security and Infra teams to validate outbound flows and data minimization before sign-off.

Our constraints: no third-party egress of raw logs, PII must be removed prior to any external transmission, retention policy starts at 30 days for traces and 365 days for audit logs. We also prefer to accept Splunk HEC endpoints but can consider Kafka if needed.

Can you share an architectural sketch and a checklist? Hoping to review by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Lydia Barnes

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: both patterns are supported; tradeoffs below and I attached a proposal sketch we can iterate on (enclave-collector-proposal-v1.pdf).

High-level options (pros/cons):

1) Customer-run collector (recommended when customer controls custody)
   - Pros: No third-party egress; full control over filtering and PII scrubbing; aligns with strict audit requirements.
   - Cons: Requires Ops effort to run/upgrade; needs compatibility testing with our trace hooks and log contract.

2) Redwood-managed hardened forwarder (hosted inside the enclave under customer tenancy)
   - Pros: Lower operational burden for your team; Redwood handles patching and connector updates; can provide signed audit bundles.
   - Cons: Some customers restrict any vendor-managed processes; we’d need Explicit egress approval and an HSM-backed key handshake.

Tradeoffs to note:
- Chain-of-custody: customer-run collectors provide the clearest custody path. If we run the forwarder, we provide signed delivery receipts and an evidence bundle (hash + timestamps) but custody is shared.
- Formats: We support Splunk HEC, Kafka, S3 (signed uploads), and HTTPS endpoints with mTLS.
- Tracing: Our trace hooks can emit sampling markers and request-id propagation; we recommend a 1-2% sampling for production unless you need full-trace SLOs.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick 30m call to decide pattern (customer-run vs Redwood-managed) — we’re available tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PT.
- If customer-run: we’ll send a compatibility checklist and an example helm/daemonset manifest.
- If Redwood-managed: provide network egress allowlist and KMS/HSM integration details for key exchange.

I attached the initial proposal (enclave-collector-proposal-v1.pdf) and a reference Drive link if you want inline diagrams.

Best,
Kimberly Park

> I attached the initial proposal (enclave-collector-proposal-v1.pdf) and a reference Drive link if you want inline diagrams.

Lydia — adding some implementation detail from the Observability side. Attached is a simple custody matrix (telemetry-custody-matrix.xlsx) and a short acceptance checklist for your SecOps team. Key notes: 

- Trace hooks & sampling: we add a lightweight SDK layer at the request ingress point that emits a request-id and service span; no payloads are mutated by default. If you need PII redaction we can enable a pre-export filter that runs in the collector.
- Minimal retention and hashing: we recommend storing raw audit logs only within the enclave for the 365d retention; exported artifacts should be pre-hashed with SHA256 and the hash stored in the enclave audit ledger.
- Evidence bundle format: signed manifest.json (timestamp, artifact-hash, scope-tag), zipped and pushed to your S3 (or to a signed HTTPS endpoint).

Acceptance checklist (high level):
- [ ] Collector is deployed (daemonset/sidecar) and configured for Splunk HEC or Kafka endpoint.
- [ ] PII redaction rules applied and tested on sample payloads.
- [ ] Outbound allowlist confirmed (CIDR + ports).
- [ ] Evidence bundle generation validated and manifest hashes verified.
- [ ] Alerting set for export failures > 5 min.

Questions for you: which endpoint protocol is preferred (Splunk HEC vs Kafka vs HTTPS/mTLS)? Also please confirm whether outbound is allowed to 10.0.0.0/24:443 (example) or if you require a proxy jump host.

If you prefer the customer-run path we can drop a starter helm chart and a pre-configured filter with PII rules. If Redwood will manage the forwarder we need your KMS contact for HSM key exchange.

Thanks — attaching the matrix and a sample manifest.

—Marissa
